## Quotation marks in the input

Sometimes, there are small problems with the input that seem to make things fail. An example is a data value that includes a single quotation mark. This is shown in the following example where a new R function (r) reads data as raw lines.

```{r}

## Quiet readr 
options(readr.show_col_types = FALSE)

## Load packages 
library(tidyverse)          ## brings in readr
library(gt)

## Raw string literal protects all quotes 
csv_text <- r"(
Hamlet,2024,2023,2022,2021,2019
Achtmaal,7,2,19,16,11
De Berk,14,16,10,15,19
De Lent,8,19,4,6,15
Helpt Elkander,5,14,2,9,17
't Kapelleke,18,18,11,8,13
Klein Zundert,9,3,3,1,14
Klein-Zundertse Heikant,,6,1,2,2
Laarheide,13,17,18,20,20
Laer-Akkermolen,2,10,12,14,7
Markt,10,15,13,3,3
Molenstraat,4,5,20,12,4
Poteind,3,1,16,19,9
Raamberg,19,11,14,4,10
Rijsbergen,15,12,13,13,16
Schijf,1,8,5,5,12
Stuivezand,17,9,17,18,5
't Stuk,12,7,7,17,6
Tiggelaar,6,4,6,7,1
Veldstraat,16,20,9,10,18
Wernhout,11,13,8,11,8
)"     ## Raw string delimiter closes here

## Read the data from the string
corso_results <- read_csv(
  file        = I(csv_text),
  na          = c("", "NA"),
  name_repair = "minimal"
)

## Examine the data in a table
gt(corso_results)

```
